title: The Sky That Learned to Grow Downward

features.name: starlight taking root
features.desc-on-touch: You touch what you thought was stone, but it holds the warmth of a star that fell and decided to stay. The roots are light still, not yet soil.

features.name: inverted rain of luminescence
features.desc-on-touch: Light falls upward through the canopy here, slower than real rain, pooling in the crowns of thoughts that never learned to think down.

features.name: the trunk that remembers sky
features.desc-on-touch: A tree growing inverted, its canopy buried deep, its roots waving where stars used to be. It has confused the directions but not forgotten either one.

features.name: convergence of vectors
features.desc-on-touch: The place where up and down have stopped arguing about which is which. A circuit of light and shadow moving in both directions at once.

features.name: the listening lichen
features.desc-on-touch: Pale growth on what might be bark or might be sky. It moves toward sound, not light. It has learned to hear the directions falling.

inscription: light has learned the grammar of roots; the sky grows downward here, and nothing falls anymore

reverie.title: REVERIE — between sky and soil at the moment they forget the
narr: You stand where light comes up through the earth like roots, and she
points at something you cannot see and says: look, the sky is learning
to grow. Her hand finds the warmth in the stone, and the warmth is
older than questions. The motes fall upward. She does not look at you
but you feel her certainty: this is how the land learns what it contains.

exits.label: downward through the turned earth back to where roots remember reaching
eastward toward where the stars are still learning to fall
westward to the margin where the sky is still deciding
